ca_4_the_swimming_hole.blurb: The Swimming Hole is a bouldering spot along Mill Creek in the San Bernardino Mountains, a short walk upstream from the Second Turnout on Highway 38. It centers on one standalone boulder with an overhanging face on one side and a slabby face on another, and it has nine problems. The range is wide: three at the very easiest level, a V0, two V1s, then a V3, a V4 and a single V6. That mix makes it workable for newer boulderers and for stronger climbers after something steep. The setting sits right beside the creek at roughly 3,100 feet.

ca_lower_tier_right_side.blurb: Lower Tier (Right Side) is a small group of routes on the Frustration Creek tier off Highway 38 in the San Bernardino Mountains, at about 4,900 feet. It has nine routes, six sport and three top-rope, running from 5.2 up to 5.10, with three of them at 5.10. The first lines sit at the far edge of an open flat, and the rest are farther up where the canyon tightens. Climbing here suits beginners as well as intermediate leaders, and some of the newer lines still have loose rock, so watch your head.

ca_boortemus_clump.blurb: Boortemus Clump is the rocky hill right behind Boortemus Boulder, in the Iceberg Boulder Area of Rattlesnake Canyon, part of Indian Cove in Joshua Tree National Park. Its nine routes are spread over several small formations and slabs around the hill, six of them sport and three trad. Grades stay in the lower and middle range: two at 5.6, three at 5.8, two at 5.9 and two at 5.10. That puts it in reach of newer leaders, with a few steadier-handed trad lines among the bolted ones.

ca_elderberry_buttress.blurb: Elderberry Buttress is a big slab high above Pine Creek Canyon near Bishop, in the Eastern Sierra, at around 7,500 feet. It is one of the three main sectors of the Scheelite Crags and PSOM Slab area, and it feels very different from the bolted modern crags elsewhere in the canyon. Of its nine routes, eight are trad and one is sport. Most climbs run five pitches or longer, and the grades cluster at 5.10, with one 5.7, one 5.9, one 5.11 and one 5.12. Getting to the base and back down takes real route-finding.

ca_hound_rock.blurb: Hound Rock is a large formation in Joshua Tree National Park's Quail Springs area, directly behind Baskerville Rock and within the Trashcan Rock Area. The east face holds several crack lines, while the west face has moderate cracks. It has nine routes, eight trad and one top-rope, from 5.7 to 5.11. Three sit at 5.9, two at 5.10 and three at 5.11, so it suits climbers comfortable placing gear on harder cracks. Many people pair it with Baskerville Rock and the White Cliffs of Dover.

ca_deadman_iv.blurb: Deadman IV is the smallest of the four bouldering sections at Deadman Summit, in the June Lake area of the Eastern Sierra, at about 8,000 feet. It sits in a small canyon farther along the dirt road than the first three sections. It has nine problems, and all are easy to moderate: six at V0, two at V1 and one V2. That keeps it within reach of newer boulderers and works for a warm-up session.

ca_karst_crag.blurb: Karst Crag is a 65-foot wall above the Marble Valley Cabin, one of five subareas in the Marble Mountain climbing zone of northwest California, at about 6,200 feet. It sits at the edge of a thick karst band. Nine routes are protected with gear, and top ropes can be rigged almost anywhere along the face. The grades skew hard: one 5.6, one 5.9, two at 5.10, three at 5.11 and two at 5.12. Climbers heading up should be comfortable with trad and alpine terrain.

ca_citadel_the.blurb: The Citadel is a big formation on the west side of Pinnacles National Park, with a wall about 400 feet high at the head of a canyon. It has nine routes of one to four pitches, five trad and four sport. Most land around 5.10, with one 5.4 line, one 5.7, one 5.9 and one 5.12, so it works for a range of multi-pitch parties. It is a commitment to reach, so plan for a full day.
